title: What If a Whole Country Ran on Clean Power? Iceland Nearly Does

scenes.text: What if a whole country ran on clean power? Iceland nearly does.
Its electricity is almost entirely renewable: around 70 percent hydropower and 30 percent geothermal.
About 90 percent of Icelandic homes are heated with hot water from underground.
In total, around 85 percent of the country's energy comes from domestic renewable sources.
The catch is oil. Road transport and the fishing industry still burn imported fossil fuels.
So even the greenest grid on Earth isn't finished. The last stretch is the hardest.
